name: Dolakha
description: Dolakha is a picturesque district located in the northern part of Janakpur Zone in Nepal, known for its rich cultural heritage and stunning mountain scenery. It is home to the ancient and revered Dolakha Bhimsen Temple, a popular pilgrimage site for Hindus, and offers breathtaking views of the majestic Gaurishankar Himalayan range. Dolakha is also recognized for its unique Newari architecture, vibrant festivals, and the production of traditional handicrafts, making it a culturally significant and captivating destination.

name: Dolakha Church
description: Dolakha Church, also known as the Shrine of Urkhu Liberty, is a significant religious site located in the Dolakha District of Nepal. This ancient Catholic church, built in the 17th century, is believed to be one of the oldest in the country. Its unique architectural style, blending Nepalese and European elements, makes it stand out among other religious structures. The church holds immense religious and cultural significance for both the local community and the wider Catholic population, as it is dedicated to the Virgin Mary and is said to grant wishes to devotees who visit.

name: Dolakha Kalinchowk Resort

This resort is renowned for its proximity to the sacred Kalinchowk Bhagwati Temple and offers awe-inspiring views of the majestic Himalayan ranges. As a significant eco-friendly destination, the resort boasts comfortable lodging, various adventure activities, and an opportunity to immerse in the local culture, ensuring an unforgettable experience in the heart of nature.

name: Dolalgath Picnic
description: Dolalgath Picnic is a serene and picturesque recreational spot nestled in the heart of the Kandy District in Sri Lanka. Renowned for its enchanting waterfall and captivating natural beauty, the picnic site offers visitors a refreshing escape from the hustle and bustle of daily life. With a rich history dating back to the British colonial era, Dolalgath Picnic signifies the perfect blend of cultural heritage and the wonders of nature, making it an ideal destination for both local and international tourists seeking tranquility and adventure.

name: Dolalghat Picnic Beach
description: Dolalghat Picnic Beach, located along the banks of the Sunkoshi River in Nepal, is a popular destination for local picnickers and day-trippers. Surrounded by lush green hills and terraced farms, the beach offers a serene and picturesque setting for relaxation and recreation. Its key features include clear river waters, pebbly beaches, and the opportunity for river activities such as swimming and boating, making it an ideal spot to enjoy nature and unwind from city life.

name: Dolanga Takura daolangagaa taakauraa
description: Dolanga Takura Daolangagaa Taakauraa is a significant cultural and historical site located in Mongolia. This unique complex consists of stacked stone structures, believed to have been used for various purposes such as astronomical observations, religious ceremonies, and burial rituals. The site's key features include its intricate patterns and designs, which are etched onto the stone surfaces, as well as its well-preserved condition despite being centuries old. Dolanga Takura Daolangagaa Taakauraa holds great significance for Mongolian heritage, providing valuable insights into the region's ancient civilizations and their ways of life.

name: Doleshwar Mahadev Temple
description:
Religious Site The Doleshwar temple is constructed in pagoda style. The temple is also known as Bimaleshwor and Sipare Mahadev and other names as per the local tongue and tradition. Inside the temple, there is a huge plain Shiva Linga (phallus). There are taps, a big idol of bull, a tall Trishul and other artifacts around with some constructions still underway.

Visiting this Shiva temple and offering milk and bel leaves to Lord Shiva is an important ritual for the Hindus or Lord Shiva devotees. The place which was unknown for thousands of years can be now called as a hidden gem. With the grace of Lord Shiva, it is an immense opportunity for the devotees to visit this sacred site and be blessed for the life time.

When you plan to visit Doleshwar, you can also visit other Shiva shrines like Ashapuri Mahadev Temple and Sanga, which are only few kilometers away. Sanga consists of Kailashnath Mahadev which is the world s tallest statue to Lord Shiva, standing 44 meters tall on a high hill. It can be an ideal day trip to visit all these shrines on a single day which can provide you an inner peace and evoke faith on god.

Doleshwar Mahadev is a temple of glory to all Hindu devotees around the world, and one must visit here to gain the ultimate religious experience, as some claim, the great opportunity to worship both the body and the head part of Lord Shiva is obtained only by the virtue acquired from multiple births.

name: Dolkar Thanka Arts
description: Dolkar Thangka Arts is a traditional Tibetan art form that specializes in creating intricate and spiritual paintings, known as Thangkas, which primarily depict deities, mandalas, and other religious subjects from Buddhism. These visually striking and symbolic works of art are not only considered spiritual tools for meditation and teaching but also serve as a bridge connecting the viewer to the rich cultural heritage and spiritual traditions of Tibet. Dolkar Thangka Arts continues to preserve and promote this ancient craft by employing traditional techniques, natural pigments, and gold, upholding the utmost respect for the sacredness and aesthetics of this revered art form.

name: Dolpo Art Gallery
description: Dolpo Art Gallery is a unique showcase of traditional Tibetan and Buddhist art, located in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal. This gallery is particularly significant as it specializes in the preservation and promotion of the endangered art forms from the remote Upper Dolpo region, providing a rare insight into this culturally rich yet often overlooked area. The gallery features an exquisite collection of Thangka paintings, sculptures, and handicrafts, all created by local artisans, thus providing a direct link to the region's rich artistic heritage and cultural traditions.

name: Dolpo Buddha Hotel
description: Nestled in the serene landscapes of Upper Dolpo, Nepal, Dolpo Buddha Hotel is a quaint yet significant establishment that offers a unique blend of traditional Tibetan architecture and modern amenities. As the only hotel in the region, it holds immense significance as a resting point for trekkers and visitors exploring the secluded beauty of the Dolpo region. The hotel's key features include cozy rooms with panoramic views of the mountains, a warm and hospitable staff, and a commitment to sustainable tourism, all of which contribute to an unforgettable Himalayan experience.

name: Dolpo Museum daolapao samgaraahalaya
description: Dolpo Museum, also known as Daolapao Samgaraahalaya, is a significant cultural institution located in the remote Upper Dolpo region of Nepal. This museum showcases the rich history, traditions, and lifestyle of the indigenous people of Dolpo, providing valuable insights into their unique culture. Its key features include a vast collection of artifacts, such as ancient tools, traditional costumes, religious relics, and thangka paintings, which offer a glimpse into the daily lives and spiritual practices of the Dolpo community. The museum's significance lies in its role as a protector and promoter of the region's cultural heritage, preserving the stories and traditions of the Dolpo people for future generations.

name: Dolpo Zhur monastery
description: Dolpo Zhur monastery, nestled in the remote Dolpo region of Nepal, is a significant religious site for the Tibetan Buddhist community. As the main monastery of the Dolpo region, it is renowned for its unique architecture, blending local and Tibetan styles, and for being home to several hundred monks. The monastery houses numerous sacred relics and thangkas, and is a vital center for preserving and promoting the region's unique cultural heritage, including the Bon and Nyingma traditions of Tibetan Buddhism.

name: Doramba Bazar (Tourist destination)
description: Doramba Bazar, located in the Dolakha district of Nepal, is a vibrant and culturally rich tourist destination. Nestled amidst the breathtaking Himalayan landscape, this bustling marketplace offers a unique blend of traditional Nepalese architecture, local handicrafts, and delectable cuisine. Doramba Bazar is particularly significant for its centuries-old history as a trading post, where Tibetan and Nepalese merchants would exchange goods, fostering a rich cultural exchange that continues to thrive today. Visitors can explore the winding streets, interact with friendly locals, and gain a deeper understanding of the region's rich heritage.

name: Doramba sailung gaupalika
description: Doramba Sailung Gaupalika is a rural municipality located in the Dolakha district of Nepal, established in 2017. It is significant as it encompasses the historic Sailung Hill, a sacred site for many ethnic communities, and is home to diverse cultures, languages, and religious practices. The gaupalika is known for its rich biodiversity, with numerous forests, rivers, and wildlife, and it aims to promote sustainable development, community-based tourism, and cultural preservation.

name: Doti
description: Doti is one of the 77 districts located in the Sudurpaschim Province of western Nepal. It is known for its rich cultural heritage, with the Chepang and Magar communities being the largest ethnic groups. Doti is also significant for its agricultural productivity, particularly in the cultivation of rice, maize, and wheat. The district is home to the beautiful Doti Lake and the scenic Chankheli Danda, making it a popular destination for tourists seeking natural beauty and cultural experiences.

name: Doti ghogatal
description: Doti Ghogatal is a traditional Nepalese dish hailing from the Doti region. It is a flavorful curry made with local ingredients like pumpkin, potato, and lentils, simmered in a unique blend of spices. The dish is known for its hearty, comforting qualities, and it showcases the region's agricultural heritage and culinary traditions. Doti Ghogatal is a testament to the rich cultural diversity of Nepalese cuisine and is a beloved staple in many households.

description: Dr. Subhash Animal Hospital & Research Center Pvt. Ltd. is a renowned veterinary facility located in Mumbai, India. Established in 1981, the hospital has been a pioneer in providing advanced veterinary care, diagnosis, and treatment for a wide range of animals. With a team of experienced veterinarians, state-of-the-art equipment, and a commitment to ethical practices, the hospital has made significant contributions to animal healthcare and research. It is known for its dedication to animal welfare, offering comprehensive services that include surgery, dentistry, internal medicine, and emergency care, making it a trusted destination for pet owners and animal lovers alike.

description: Dream Park is a renowned, immersive amusement park that combines cutting-edge technology with storytelling and interactive experiences to create a unique blend of entertainment and education. By harnessing these advanced features, Dristi significantly improves customer engagement, satisfaction, and loyalty, ultimately driving business growth and success in today's competitive market.

Duda's significance lies in its focus on facilitating web design for agencies, designers, and resellers, allowing them to efficiently cater to clients and scale their businesses.

name: Dudamukh Baghkhor Park
description: Dudamukh Baghkhor Park is a picturesque green space located in the heart of Sylhet, Bangladesh. Known for its vibrant seasonal flower gardens and tranquil ambiance, the park is a popular destination for both locals and tourists seeking relaxation and recreation. A significant feature of the park is the large lake, home to a variety of aquatic life, which offers boat rides for visitors to enjoy the serene beauty of the park from a different perspective. The park also hosts cultural events and festivals, making it a vital community hub that celebrates the rich heritage and tradition of the region.

name: Dudh Pokhari daudha paokharaii
description: Dudh Pokhari Daudha Paokharai is a community-based festival celebrated in the western region of Nepal, particularly in the Dang district. The festival revolves around the revered Dudh Pokhari pond, where devotees take a holy bath to cleanse their sins and pray for peace, prosperity, and good health. This unique event features traditional music, cultural dances, and various recreational activities, fostering unity, and social harmony among the diverse communities participating in the festivities.

name: Dudh daha
description: Dudh Daha is a serene freshwater lake situated in the Chitwan District of Nepal, known for its picturesque natural beauty and tranquil surroundings. The lake is renowned for its rich biodiversity, particularly the diverse aquatic life, including various species of fish, and is a significant local site for religious and cultural activities. Dudh Daha's captivating landscape, with its crystal-clear waters, lush greenery, and the backdrop of the Himalayas, makes it an ideal destination for nature enthusiasts and peace-seekers alike.

name: Dudhauli park
description: Dudhauli Park is a significant protected area in Nepal, located in the Rautahat district. Known for its rich biodiversity, the park spans over 1,665 hectares and serves as an essential habitat for various wildlife species, including the endangered Asian Elephant. Its key features include a large artificial lake, lush Sal forests, and grasslands, providing a perfect setting for activities such as boating, birdwatching, and jungle safari, making it a popular destination for nature enthusiasts and conservationists.

name: Dudhkoshi Chhirdi Motorable Bridge
description: The Dudhkoshi Chhirdi Motorable Bridge, located in Nepal, is a significant engineering marvel that spans the mighty Dudhkoshi River. This bridge is notable for being the first motorable bridge in the region, providing crucial access and connectivity for local communities and trekkers along the Everest Base Camp route. With a total length of 350 meters, it features a sturdy suspension design capable of withstanding the harsh Himalayan climate and the weight of heavy vehicles, thereby playing a pivotal role in the economic development and tourism of the area.

name: Dudhkunda Adventure Treks
description: Dudhkunda Adventure Treks is a renowned trekking company based in Nepal, known for providing high-quality and personalized trekking experiences in the Himalayas. With a strong emphasis on safety, sustainability, and cultural immersion, Dudhkunda Adventure Treks offers a wide range of itineraries that cater to all fitness levels and interests, from the classic Everest Base Camp trek to off-the-beaten-path adventures in remote regions. The company's experienced guides and support staff are dedicated to ensuring that every client has a memorable and life-changing journey in the stunning landscapes of the Nepalese Himalayas.

name: Dudhpokhari gaupalika lamjung
description: Dudhpokhari Gaupalika is a local government unit located in Lamjung district of Gandaki Province in Nepal. It was established in 2017 as part of the country's decentralization reforms, and it includes several wards spread across an area known for its natural beauty and cultural heritage. The gaupalika is home to the scenic Dudhpokhari lake, which is a popular tourist destination, and it is also rich in biodiversity with several protected forests and wildlife reserves. The local economy is based on agriculture, tourism, and small-scale enterprises, and the gaupalika is committed to promoting sustainable development, community empowerment, and good governance

name: Dudiley Tol
description: Dudiley Tol is a fictional, enchanted forest introduced in J.K. Rowling's Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald. This mystical forest serves as a crucial location in the story, inhabited by various magical creatures. Its key feature is the sentient, ancient tree called the "Dumbledore's Fountain of Magic," which holds the power to reveal the true master of the Elder Wand. The forest's significance lies in its role as a symbol of the magical world's hidden depths and the interconnectedness of powerful magical artifacts and beings.

name: Dugahiti
description: Dugahiti is a notable cave system located in the Philippines, known for its breathtaking beauty and significant archaeological value. It features an extensive network of limestone caverns adorned with stunning stalactites, stalagmites, and other calcite formations. The cave system holds great historical importance as it has provided valuable insights into prehistoric human activity, with findings of ancient tools, art, and pottery, offering a glimpse into the lives of early Filipino inhabitants.

name: Dugure Ground
description: Dugure Ground is a significant historical site located in the Lower Omo Valley of Ethiopia. It is renowned for its well-preserved rock art, featuring various motifs such as animals, humans, and abstract shapes. These engravings and paintings provide valuable insights into the culture, lifestyle, and beliefs of ancient communities that inhabited the region, making Dugure Ground an essential destination for archaeologists and history enthusiasts.

name: Duhabi (dauhawaii) Saptari
description: Duhabi, also known as Dauhawaii, is a small municipality located in the Saptari district of southeastern Nepal. It is situated along the banks of the Mahananda River and is known for its rich cultural heritage and religious significance. The area is home to several ancient temples and shrines, including the famous Duhabi Mai temple, which attracts many devotees and tourists throughout the year. Additionally, Duhabi is known for its agricultural productivity, with rice, wheat, and maize being the primary crops grown in the region.

name: Duhabi suspension bridge
description: The Duhabi Suspension Bridge, located in Eastern Nepal, is a significant engineering feat showcasing the region's unique craftsmanship. Spanning approximately 560 feet over the Koshi River, it's one of the longest suspension bridges in the country. Its key features include locally sourced materials like ropes made from natural fibers and wooden planks for the walking surface, demonstrating sustainable building practices. The bridge holds immense cultural significance as it serves as a vital link between two rural communities, facilitating trade, social interactions, and access to essential services.

name: Dulal Gaun Namuna Pratikshyalaya
description: Dulal Gaun Namuna Pratikshyalaya, also known as Dulal Gaun Model Observatory, is a significant astronomical institution located in Dulal Gaun, Kavrepalanchok District, Nepal. Established in 2014, it is the first model observatory in the country, providing a unique platform for students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts to observe celestial bodies. The observatory is equipped with a 16-inch telescope, the largest of its kind in Nepal, and offers regular observation sessions, workshops, and training programs, promoting astronomical education and fostering a deeper understanding of the universe.

name: Dullu Museum
description: Dullu Museum, located in Dullu, Nepal, is a significant cultural institution that showcases the rich history and heritage of the region. The museum's key features include a vast collection of archaeological artifacts, sculptures, coins, and other historical objects, many of which date back to the ancient Licchavi and Malla periods. Its significance lies in its role as a vital resource for understanding the historical and cultural development of the western Nepal region, as well as its contribution to the preservation and promotion of the country's cultural heritage.

name: Dumping side of Deumai Municipality, Ilam
description: The Dumping side of Deumai Municipality in Ilam is a significant area that serves as the primary waste disposal site for the local community. It is characterized by large mounds of mixed solid waste, including household, commercial, and agricultural debris. Despite its negative environmental impacts, the dumping site plays a crucial role in maintaining the cleanliness and hygiene of the surrounding areas by providing a designated location for waste disposal. However, there is a growing need for proper waste management strategies and techniques to minimize its environmental footprint and promote sustainable waste disposal practices.

name: Dumraha Duhabi 10
description: Dumraha Duhabi 10 is a significant archaeological site located in the Terai region of Nepal. It is known for its well-preserved brick structures, terracotta figurines, and inscribed bricks dating back to the Licchavi period (4th to 8th century CE), providing valuable insights into the art, culture, and administration of ancient Nepal. The site's significance lies in its contribution to understanding the evolution of urban settlements, religious practices, and societal structures during this formative period of Nepalese history.

name: Dumsheree Gorkha
description: Dumsheree Gorkha is a small village in the Ilam district of Nepal, known for its stunning natural beauty and rich cultural heritage. The village is predominantly inhabited by the Gorkha community, who are renowned for their bravery and contributions to military services worldwide. Dumsheree Gorkha is significant for its traditional architecture, vibrant festivals, and unique agro-based lifestyle, which offers visitors a glimpse into the authentic Nepalese culture and the Gorkha way of life.

name: Dunai
description: Dunai, also known as the Karnali River, is the longest and largest river in Nepal, originating from the glaciers of Mount Kailash in Tibet. It is revered in Hinduism and Buddhism, and its name translates to 'black' in local languages, reflecting its dark waters. The Dunai plays a significant role in Nepal's hydropower potential, irrigation, and biodiversity, while also offering thrilling white-water rafting experiences.

name: Duner Temple Vatagau
description: Duner Temple Vatagau is an ancient and revered religious site located in the heart of the Duner desert. This architectural marvel is known for its grandiose structure, featuring intricate sandstone carvings and towering spires that reach skyward. The temple holds immense significance for local Duner tribes, who believe it to be the sacred dwelling of their divine protectors. Pilgrims from far and wide journey to Vatagau to seek blessings, wisdom, and healing, making it a focal point of cultural and spiritual life in the region.

name: Dupcheshwor Mahadev Mandir
description: Dupcheshwor Mahadev Mandir is an ancient and highly revered Hindu temple located in Baglung District, Nepal. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, this temple is unique for its natural shiva lingam formation, which is submerged in water and can be seen only during the dry season. The temple is also significant for its cultural and religious heritage, as it hosts various festivals and attracts thousands of devotees every year.

name: Durbar Adventure Zipline Resort
description: Durbar Adventure Zipline Resort is an exciting eco-tourism destination located in the lush green hills of Nepal, offering a thrilling zipline experience that provides breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape. As the first of its kind in the region, this resort holds significant value in promoting adventure tourism and contributing to local economic development while preserving the natural environment. The resort's zipline, spanning over 1.8 kilometers, is one of the longest and most exhilarating in Asia, making it a must-visit attraction for adventure seekers and nature enthusiasts alike.

name: Durbar Devisthan (Gulmi Durbar)
description: Durbar Devisthan, also known as Gulmi Durbar, is a historic palace complex located in Tamghas, Gulmi district of Nepal. It was the royal residence of the Sen kings who ruled the region from the 16th to 18th centuries. The complex showcases intricate Newari architecture, featuring numerous temples, courtyards, and a museum that exhibits artifacts from the Sen dynasty. Durbar Devisthan holds significant historical and cultural value, reflecting the rich heritage of the Gulmi region and the artistic brilliance of the Newar craftsmen.

name: Durga Mandir Kalyanpur
description: Durga Mandir Kalyanpur is a renowned Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Durga, located in Kanpur, India. The temple is known for its striking architecture, featuring intricate carvings and sculptures of various Hindu deities. Durga Mandir Kalyanpur holds significant religious importance, particularly during the Navratri festival when thousands of devotees gather to offer their prayers and seek the blessings of Goddess Durga. The temple's serene atmosphere and spiritual aura make it a prominent pilgrimage site for followers of Hinduism.

name: Durga Mandir Rangeli
description: Durga Mandir Rangeli is an ancient and highly revered Hindu temple, located in the Rangeli village of Bihar, India. Dedicated to Goddess Durga, the temple showcases intricate and exquisite architectural craftsmanship, with its multi-tiered roof and sculptures of various Hindu deities. The temple is considered a significant religious site, particularly during the Navratri festival when thousands of devotees gather to offer their prayers and participate in the traditional celebrations.

name: Durga Mandir, Laxmipur, Balara-3, Sarlahi, Nepal
description: Durga Mandir in Laxmipur, Balara-3, Sarlahi, Nepal, is a highly venerated Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Durga. The temple is renowned for its striking architecture, featuring a nine-tiered pagoda-style roof, intricate woodcarvings, and vibrant colors. Durga Mandir holds immense religious significance, as it is believed to be a powerful abode of the goddess, attracting thousands of devotees annually, particularly during the Navaratri festival, to seek blessings and spiritual solace.

name: Durga Temple
description: Durga Temple, also known as the Monkey Temple, is a prominent 16th-century Hindu temple located in Hampi, India. Dedicated to the goddess Durga, it is celebrated for its unique architectural style that blends Dravidian and Vijayanagara elements. The temple's key features include a towering gateway, intricate carvings depicting various Hindu deities, and a large statue of the goddess herself. Its significance lies in being a testament to the religious and cultural richness of the Vijayanagara Empire, as well as a popular pilgrimage site for devotees of Durga.

name: Durga bhawani mandir
description: Durga Bhawani Mandir is a prominent Hindu temple located in the historic city of Kota, Rajasthan, India. Dedicated to Goddess Durga, the temple is renowned for its architectural grandeur and spiritual significance. The key features of the temple include a grand entrance gate, intricately carved idols, and a serene ambiance that attracts devotees and tourists alike. Durga Bhawani Mandir holds immense religious importance, especially during the Navratri festival when it is adorned with vibrant colors and lights, and thousands of devotees gather to seek the blessings of the divine Goddess.

name: Durga mandir (Temple), Lalbandi ,Sarlahi
description: Durga Mandir in Lalbandi, Sarlahi is a renowned Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Durga. Known for its architectural beauty and religious significance, the temple attracts thousands of devotees every year, particularly during the Navaratri festival. The temple's key features include a pond, intricate carvings, and a peaceful atmosphere, making it a spiritually serene place for worship and reflection.

name: Durga mandir bichpatti
description: Durga Mandir, located in Bichpatti, is a renowned Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Durga. The temple is known for its intricate and vibrant architecture, showcasing a fusion of Mughal and Hindu styles. Durga Mandir holds great religious significance, especially during Navratri, when devotees from far and wide flock to offer their prayers and seek the blessings of the goddess. The temple's peaceful atmosphere and serene surroundings make it an ideal place for spiritual reflection and communion with the divine.

name: Durgapur Jhapa
description: Durgapur Jhapa is a significant town located in the eastern part of Nepal, in the Jhapa District. It is known for its lush green tea gardens, making it a major contributor to Nepal's tea industry. The town is also recognized for its religious diversity, housing various temples and monasteries, which reflects the harmonious coexistence of different cultures and communities in the region.

name: Durgathali
description: Durgathali is a small yet spiritually significant village located in the Bankura district of West Bengal, India. It is renowned for its ancient Durga Temple, which is believed to be over 250 years old and is an excellent example of traditional Bengali terracotta architecture. The temple attracts numerous devotees and tourists during the Durga Puja festival, as it showcases intricate terracotta carvings depicting various mythological stories, making it a living testament to the region's rich cultural heritage.

name: Durlung Kot
description: Durlung Kot is an ancient fort located in the Durlung village of Kavrepalanchok district in Nepal. The fort, perched atop a hill, is believed to date back to the Licchavi period (4th to 8th centuries) and is a testament to the country's rich historical and architectural heritage. Its key features include intricate stone carvings, a temple dedicated to Goddess Mahalaxmi, and panoramic views of the surrounding countryside, making it a culturally significant site that attracts both local pilgrims and tourists.

name: Earthquake Memorial Statue
description: The Earthquake Memorial Statue stands as a solemn tribute to the lives lost in seismic tragedies. Its key features include a bronze sculpture of hands reaching upwards from twisted rubble, symbolizing resilience and hope amidst destruction. The statue's significance lies in its ability to evoke reflection on the power of nature and the strength of human spirit, serving as a reminder of the importance of preparedness and commemoration for those affected by earthquakes.

name: Earthquake Memorial park
description: Earthquake Memorial Park, located in Mexico City, is a significant public space dedicated to the victims of the devastating 1985 earthquake. The park's key features include the iconic "Tree of Life" sculpture, a poignant symbol of resilience and rebirth, and the "Silent Bell," which tolls every year on the anniversary of the disaster. Surrounded by lush greenery, the memorial serves as a serene gathering place for reflection and commemoration, emphasizing the city's strength and unity in the face of adversity.

name: East-west Highway Birtamod
description: The East-West Highway Birtamod is a significant transportation infrastructure in eastern Nepal, connecting the Indian border town of Jogbani to the western region of the country. This 92-kilometer-long highway is a key component of the Asian Highway Network, facilitating seamless cross-border trade, tourism, and transportation between Nepal and India. The highway is also notable for its role in promoting socio-economic development in the region by reducing travel time and costs, improving accessibility to essential services, and fostering greater regional integration.

name: Jagannath temple
description:
Heritage Site The ancient evidence says that King Bhupatindra Malla is responsible for the erection of the Chardham temples of Bhaktapur. Along with the Jagannath temple, he also commenced the Badrinath temple, Kedarnath temple, and Rameshwar temple.
Yes, however, this Jagannath temple consists of a place among char Dham temples.
The current temple of Jagannath seems quite ordinary covered with a tin roof. This one-story temple was three times bigger and of two stories on its erection. The ruinous earthquake of 1934 A.D. somehow spectacularly affects the physical appearance of this temple.
Nowadays, we can see a simple architecture assembled over there. So, it can protect the beautiful wood sculptures of Lord Krishna, Balaram, and Subhadra, erected inside the temple.
Image of Jagannath
The Jagana God Jatra
This, Jagana God Jatra is a very minor jatra of Bhaktapur. That is not forgotten continuously now. According to the events of the lunar year, this event falls on the second day of Dillathwa.
Yonder, dillathwa means the starting days of the ninth month, as of the Nepal sambat. On the occasion of the day, the statue of Jagannath is worshipped by its Pujari. That, with a special ritual. Meanwhile, a small group of people carries away the diety to roam the city.

name: Jalbinayak Mandir
description:
The Jal Binayak Temple is a revered Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Ganesh, situated in the Chobhar area of Kathmandu, Nepal. It stands as one of the four principal Ganesh temples in the Kathmandu Valley, alongside Chandra Binayak, Surya Binayak, and Ashok Binayak.Historical Background:

The temple's origins trace back to 723 Nepal Sambat (NS), during the reign of King Shiva Singh Malla, who initially constructed the temple. In 789 NS, King Sri Nivas Malla of Patan enhanced the structure by adding a gold-plated Gajur (the pinnacle of the temple). The current pagoda-style architecture was established in 871 NS by King Rajya Prakash Malla of Kathmandu.Cultural Significance:

Jal Binayak Temple holds profound cultural and religious importance, especially during the festival of Ganesh Chaturthi, when devotees gather to honor Lord Ganesh. The temple's architecture, featuring traditional pagoda design, reflects the rich heritage of Nepalese craftsmanship.

It typically involves guided tours through national parks or game reserves, often conducted in open-top vehicles or on foot, allowing visitors to witness a variety of animals, from majestic elephants and graceful gazelles to elusive tigers and lions, in their natural behaviors and ecological interactions. This experience fosters appreciation for biodiversity, promotes conservation efforts, and provides unforgettable memories amidst the raw beauty of the jungle.

name: Junichande
description: Junichede is a unique and intricate system of timekeeping in Japan, which divides a day into ten main periods, or "shifts" (On), further subdivided into six smaller units. It was predominantly used during the Edo period (1603-1868) in urban areas for various purposes, such as regulating work and social activities. The precision and structure of Junichede highlight the importance of time management and organization in Japanese culture, demonstrating a fascinating historical alternative to the more widely adopted 12-hour clock system.

name: Jure Chhango
description: Jure Chhango, also known as the "Lake Taleju Massacre," refers to a tragic event that occurred in Nepal on May 23, 2001. During a royal dinner at the Narayanhiti Palace, Crown Prince Dipendra shot and killed several members of the royal family before turning the gun on himself. Jure Chhango resulted in the death of ten people, including King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya, and marked a turning point in Nepal's history, leading to the abolition of the monarchy and the establishment of a federal democratic republic in 2008. The incident remains a significant and controversial event in Nepal'

name: Kaiser Mahal Palace
description:
Historical Ruins Kaiser Mahal is a historic Rana palace located in Kathmandu, Nepal, west of the Narayanhiti Palace. Originally built in 1895 for Kaiser Shamsher Jang Bahadur Rana, the palace complex features an impressive array of courtyards, gardens, and buildings, showcasing unique Edwardian architectural elements.
Historically significant, Kaiser Mahal has undergone various changes since the fall of the Rana regime. It was sold to the Government of Nepal and now houses the Kaiser Library and the Public Procurement Monitoring Office. The library, established by Kaiser Shamsher, contains around 28,000 volumes and serves as both a library and a small museum showcasing his extensive collection of books and artifacts.
The palace was partially damaged during the April 2015 earthquake but has since undergone retrofitting to preserve its historical architecture while enhancing safety standards. As of June 2024, it has been fully operational as a government office following extensive renovations.

The park provides panoramic views of the Kathmandu Valley, including the Ganesh Himal and Langtang Lirung mountain ranges.

Kajin Sara Lake holds cultural significance for local communities and has recently gained attention as a popular destination for adventure tourism, offering trekkers the opportunity to experience Nepal's pristine natural beauty. name: Kali Mandir
description: Religious Site The most iconic venue of Biratnagar, it is also regarded as the guardian deity of the City. The Kalisthan or Kali Mandir was transferred or derived from the older Kali Mandir in Rangeli in around 1915 AD or 1972 BS when the headquarter of the earnest while Morang District was shifted from Rangeli to Biratnagar. This temple, along with the District Office and Land Revenue office were relocated into the newer Biratnagar city, thus encouraging locals to come and settle in the new city. The older temple is still situated in the city of Rangeli. The temple is the center place of worship during the Dashain festivals when people line up for hours infront of the temple during the 7th to 9th of the Dashain festival. There is an altar for sacrificing animals during the event.The temple was revamped into its current form in early 2000 and has since retained the traditional pagoda styled roof at the top and is cladded with marbles on its facades. There is a central temple, an altar, space for conducting prayers and also a seven decade old Dharmashala in its backyard. The temple also has its numerous and iconic bells which are regularly rung during the evening 'Aarati' (prayer). It is located right into the heart of the oldest and most vibrant market of Biratnagar in the Bazaradda.

While tradition once saw animal sacrifices performed within the temple grounds, a shift towards compassion has prevailed. In 2016, the sacrificial practice of pigeons was replaced by their symbolic release, a testament to the temple's embrace of a gentler, more peaceful form of devotion. Kanchenjunga Conservation Area is a protected area in the Himalayas of eastern Nepal that was established in 1997. It covers 2,035 km2 (786 sq mi) in the Taplejung District and comprises two peaks of Kanchenjunga. In the north it adjoins the Qomolangma National Nature Preserve in Tibet, and in the east the Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim. To the west it borders the Sankhuwasabha District. It ranges in altitude from 1,200 to 8,586 m (3,937 to 28,169 ft). It is part of the Sacred Himalayan Landscape, which is being developed by WWF Nepal in partnership with the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.

When the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area was designated in March 1997, it was Nepal's third Conservation Area. In April 2003, a Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Management Council was formed with the support of WWF Nepal, comprising seven Conservation Area User Committees, 44 User Groups, and 32 Mother Groups. These community based institutions support effective implementation of all planned activities. In August 2006, the Government of Nepal handed over the management of the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area to the Management Council.

Kanu Chowk is a notable intersection located in Birgunj, a metropolitan city in the Parsa District of Nepal. Birgunj, often referred to as the "Gateway of Nepal," serves as a significant commercial hub, facilitating trade and commerce between Nepal and India.The chowk (meaning "intersection" or "square" in Nepali) is a bustling area characterized by a variety of shops, markets, and eateries, reflecting the vibrant economic activity of the city. It serves as a central point for transportation, with numerous vehicles and pedestrians passing through daily.

The name "Kanu" is associated with a community present in the region, contributing to the cultural diversity of Birgunj.

name: Kanyam
description: Kanyam, situated in the Ilam District of eastern Nepal, is a picturesque town celebrated for its expansive tea gardens, earning it the moniker "Queen of Eastern Nepal.he region's lush green landscapes and temperate climate make it a favored destination for both domestic and international tourists seeking tranquility and natural beauty. Visitors can explore the well-maintained tea estates, observe the traditional tea-picking process, and even participate in tea tasting sessions, gaining insight into Nepal's tea culture. Beyond its tea gardens, Kanyam offers various recreational activities, including horseback riding and nature walks, allowing tourists to immerse themselves in the serene environment. The town's proximity to the Nepal-India border enhances its accessibility, attracting visitors from neighboring countriesdditionally, Kanyam's rich cultural heritage is reflected in the harmonious coexistence of various ethnic groups, each contributing to the vibrant cultural tapestry of the region. The area's cool climate, panoramic views, and cultural richness make Kanyam a must-visit destination for those exploring eastern Nepal.

name: Kapersthan Mahankal Hike Point
description: Kapersthan Mahankal Hike Point, located in the Kavrepalanchok District of Nepal, is a notable destination for trekking enthusiasts seeking a blend of natural beauty and cultural significance. The hike offers panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes, including rolling hills and verdant forests, providing a serene environment for nature lovers. Along the trail, trekkers can experience the rich cultural heritage of the local communities, with opportunities to visit traditional villages and observe daily life. The Mahankal Temple, dedicated to Lord Mahankal, is a significant landmark along the route, adding a spiritual dimension to the journey. The temple is known for its historical importance and is a place of worship for both locals and visitors. The hike is accessible from Kathmandu, making it a convenient option for those looking to explore the natural and cultural offerings of Nepal. For accommodations, there are several options near the Kapersthan Mahankal Hike Point, ranging from local guesthouses to more established hotels, catering to different preferences and budgets.

name: Kapil Himal
description: Kapil Himal, located in the far western region of Nepal, is a prominent mountain in the Dhaulagiri range, standing at approximately 7,462 meters (24,482 feet) above sea level. This peak is renowned for its challenging terrain and is a coveted destination for experienced mountaineers seeking to test their skills in high-altitude environments. The mountain offers breathtaking views of the surrounding landscapes, including the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges, providing trekkers and climbers with a profound sense of accomplishment upon reaching its summit. Due to its remote location and technical demands, expeditions to Kapil Himal require meticulous planning and are typically undertaken by seasoned climbers with prior high-altitude experience. The journey to Kapil Himal also offers an opportunity to explore the rich cultural heritage of the local communities, who maintain traditional lifestyles amidst the rugged terrain. For those interested in undertaking an expedition to Kapil Himal, it is advisable to consult with experienced trekking agencies and local guides to ensure safety and a rewarding experience.

name: Kapilvastu Avinash Church
description: Kapilvastu Eternal Church, also known as Avinash Church, is a Christian place of worship located in the Kapilvastu District of Nepal. The church serves as a spiritual center for the local Christian community, offering regular services and fellowship opportunities. Weekly gatherings are held on Saturdays at 12 noon, and prayer meetings take place on Wednesdays at 8 pm. The church also engages in various community activities, including cultural events that showcase the rich traditions of the Tharu people, such as performances during Christmas programs.

name: Kapilvastu Museum
description:
Kapilvastu Museum, situated in Tilaurakot, Nepal, is a cultural and religious institution dedicated to preserving the rich history of the ancient city of Kapilvastu, the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama, who later became known as the Buddha. The museum houses a diverse collection of artifacts, including terracotta vessels, copper coins, and other items dating back to the 7th century BC, offering valuable insights into the region's archaeological and cultural heritage.The museum's exhibits are meticulously curated to showcase the art and artifacts discovered at various archaeological sites within the ancient Kapilvastu territory, such as Tilaurakot, Niglihawa, Gotihawa, Arorakot, Sisahaniyakot, Chhetradehi, Sagrahawa, and Pipari. These sites have yielded numerous ancient art remains and monuments, many of which are on display at the museum, providing visitors with a comprehensive understanding of the area's historical significance.Visitors to the Kapilvastu Museum can explore its well-organized galleries, which feature a range of artifacts that illuminate the daily life, religious practices, and artistic achievements of the ancient inhabitants of Kapilvastu. The museum serves as an essential resource for scholars, students, and tourists interested in the history of Buddhism and the cultural evolution of the region.

For those planning a visit, the museum is located approximately 26 kilometers from Lumbini, the birthplace of Lord Buddha, making it a convenient addition to a pilgrimage or cultural tour of the area.
address: C4QH+MGJ, Piprahawa - Bankatwa Rd, Pachangawa, Uttar Pradesh 272202, bhaarata

name: Kapilvastu Park - Ancient Buddhist Site
description: Kapilvastu Park, located in the Kapilvastu District of Nepal, is an ancient Buddhist site of profound historical and cultural significance. This area was once the capital of the Shakya Kingdom, where Siddhartha Gautama, who later became the Buddha, spent his early years. The park encompasses the ruins of the ancient city of Kapilavastu, including remnants of palaces, temples, and other structures that offer a glimpse into the life and times of the Buddha. Archaeological excavations have uncovered artifacts such as pottery, coins, and inscriptions, providing valuable insights into the region's rich history. Visitors to Kapilvastu Park can explore these historical sites, reflecting on the early life of the Buddha and the cultural heritage of the Shakya people. The park is situated approximately 25 kilometers southwest of Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha, making it a significant destination for those interested in Buddhist history and archaeology.
address: C4XH+63W, National Highway 233, Birdpur No.1, Uttar Pradesh 272202, bhaarata

name: Kapilvastu arghakhanchi border
description: The Kapilvastu-Arghakhanchi border delineates the northern boundary of Kapilvastu District and the southern boundary of Arghakhanchi District in Nepal. This border region is characterized by diverse topography, including the Banganga River, which flows transnationally from Arghakhanchi into Kapilvastu and eventually merges with the Ganges in Uttar Pradesh, India. The river holds significant religious importance for Buddhist pilgrims, as it is believed that Siddhartha Gautama, who later became the Buddha, rode his horse along its banks when he left his palace to seek enlightenment.The area is also notable for Surya Odhar, a cave near the border that is associated with the Buddha's early life. However, this site is in need of development to enhance its accessibility and preservation.For travelers and pilgrims, the border area offers a unique opportunity to explore sites of historical and cultural significance, including the ancient city of Kapilavastu, the birthplace of the Buddha. The region's rich history and natural beauty make it a noteworthy destination for those interested in Nepal's Buddhist heritage.

name: Kapra village
description: Kapra is a locality situated in the Jayaprithivi area of Bajhang District, Sudurpashchim Pradesh, Nepal. Located at an elevation of approximately 2,127 meters, Kapra offers panoramic views of the surrounding mountainous terrain. The area is characterized by its natural beauty, including lush forests and diverse wildlife, making it a potential destination for eco-tourism and trekking enthusiasts. The village is accessible via local roads connecting to the district headquarters, and visitors can experience the traditional lifestyle of the local communities.

name: Karnali Conservation Center
description: The Karnali Conservation Center is dedicated to preserving the biodiversity of Nepal's Karnali region, focusing on the Ganges River dolphin population in the Karnali River system. Established in 1994, it has expanded to twelve branches, offering school outreach programs and serving as a research base for conservationists. These efforts have led to a two-fold increase in dolphin abundance and heightened educational awareness in the region.Additionally, the Upper Karnali Landscape Initiative documents biodiversity and promotes community participation in wildlife conservation in the Upper Karnali region, home to species like the wild yak, snow leopard, and Himalayan wolf. This initiative employs a community-led, multi-faceted approach to conservation.

name: Karnali U-Turn,Bijaura
description: Karnali U-Turn, located near Bijaura in Surkhet District, Karnali Province, Nepal, is a scenic spot where the Karnali River makes a dramatic bend, offering breathtaking views of the river as it winds through lush green valleys and majestic hills.This area is ideal for photography, hiking, and bird watching, with trails that wind through the picturesque landscape, offering glimpses of diverse wildlife and the chance to connect with nature.Visitors can also interact with local communities to learn about their traditions and partake in regional festivities.

name: Karpureshwar Park
description:
Karpureshwar Park is a serene recreational area located in Besisahar, the district headquarters of Lamjung District in Gandaki Province, Nepal. Situated near the confluence of the Marsyangdi and Khudi rivers, the park offers picturesque views of the surrounding hills and rivers, making it an ideal spot for relaxation and photography.

Visitors can enjoy leisurely walks along the riverbanks, engage in local cultural activities, and explore nearby attractions such as the Karpureshwar Mandir, a revered Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. The park's tranquil environment provides a peaceful retreat for both locals and tourists.

name: Karuna AG Church
description:
Assembly of God Karuna Church is a Christian place of worship located in Belganar, Dang District, Nepal. The church is part of the global Assemblies of God fellowship, known for its Pentecostal beliefs and practices.

In addition to its religious services, the church is involved in community activities, including cultural events. For instance, a Christian Sorathi dance was performed at the church, showcasing the integration of cultural expressions within the church community.

name: Karyabinayak Mandir
description: Karyabinayak Mandir is a revered Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Ganesh, situated in Bungamati, Lalitpur District, approximately 10 kilometers south of Kathmandu, Nepal. Constructed in 1661 AD under the leadership of Purna Singh from Bungamati, the temple has stood the test of time, attracting countless devotees who seek the blessings of success.The temple is renowned for its intricate architecture, featuring a pagoda-style structure adorned with detailed wood carvings and metalwork. The main shrine houses a statue of Lord Ganesh, the remover of obstacles, and is a focal point for devotees, especially during Ganesh Chaturthi, a significant festival in the Hindu calendar. Visitors to Karyabinayak Mandir can experience the rich cultural heritage of the Kathmandu Valley, as the temple is located in Bungamati, a traditional Newar settlement known for its craftsmanship and historical significance. The area offers a glimpse into the traditional lifestyle and architecture of the Newar community.

name: Kashitar Park and Picnic spot
description: Kashitar Park and Picnic Spot is a recreational area located in Kashitar, Jiling, Nepal. The park is open year-round, 24/7, offering visitors a serene environment to relax and enjoy nature.

name: Kaski Nepal
description:
Kaski is a district in Gandaki Province, Nepal, renowned for its natural beauty and cultural heritage. The district encompasses the city of Pokhara, a major tourist destination celebrated for its stunning mountain views, serene lakes, and adventure sports.

Geography and Attractions:

Annapurna Region: Kaski serves as the gateway to the Annapurna Circuit, one of the world's most popular trekking routes, offering trekkers diverse landscapes and panoramic mountain vistas.

Pokhara: The district's capital, Pokhara, is known for attractions like Phewa Lake, Sarangkot, and the International Mountain Museum. The city also offers opportunities for paragliding, boating, and exploring caves.

Natural Resources: Kaski is rich in rivers such as Seti Gandaki, Modi, and Madi, along with other rivulets, contributing to its lush landscapes and agricultural productivity

name: Kaskikot Kalika Temple
description:
Kaskikot Kalika Temple is a revered Hindu shrine situated atop a hill in Kaskikot, a village in the Kaski District of Nepal. The temple is dedicated to Goddess Kali, a principal deity in Hinduism. Visitors can reach the temple by hiking from Pokhara, approximately 18 kilometers away. Historical Significance:

The area around the temple was once a fort in the 15th century, often referred to as the Kaskikot Palace. Remnants of this fort, including ramparts, still exist near the larger Kalika Temple, offering dramatic views of the Annapurna Mountains. Visiting the Temple:

The hike to Kaskikot Kalika Temple is a popular activity for both pilgrims and tourists. The trail is largely undeveloped, unpaved, and unmarked, providing a more authentic experience. At the top of the ridge, there are two lookout points: one with a small Shiva shrine and a larger lookout point with the Kali temple to the west. The temple offers panoramic views of the surrounding valleys and mountains, making it a serene spot for reflection and meditation.

name: Kaskikot Palace
description:
Kaskikot Palace is a historic landmark situated in the serene hills of Kaskikot, Nepal, offering panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Once the residence of the local kings, the palace stands as a testament to Nepal's royal heritage and architectural prowess.Historical Significance:

Before the unification of Nepal, the region was divided into several small principalities. Kaskikot was one of these, ruled by Kulmandan Shah. His descendant, Drabya Shah, later established the Kingdom of Gorkha, marking the beginning of the legendary Gorkha warriors. Visiting the Palace:

The palace is accessible via a hike from Pokhara, approximately 18 kilometers away. The trail leads to stone ruins and a shrine, offering hikers a glimpse into the area's rich history. The hike provides stunning views of the Annapurna mountain range and the Pokhara Valley.

name: Kasthamandapa
description:
Kasthamandap is a historic three-story pagoda-style structure located in Kathmandu Durbar Square, Nepal. The name "Kasthamandap" translates to "wood-covered shelter," reflecting its original construction from a single tree. It is believed to have been built in the 7th century during the Lichhavi era, though some sources suggest it was constructed in the 12th century. 


Historical Significance:

Kasthamandap is not only an architectural marvel but also holds cultural importance. It is said to have been built by Lila Vajra, and there is a shrine consecrated to Gorakshanath situated at Maru, Kathmandu. 

2015 Nepal Earthquake and Reconstruction:

On April 25, 2015, Kasthamandap was severely damaged and collapsed due to the devastating earthquake. Subsequent excavations revealed that the original structure was built in the 7th century. The reconstruction efforts aimed to restore its historical and cultural significance, and the temple was reopened to the public after extensive restoration work. 


Visiting Kasthamandap:

Kasthamandap is situated in the heart of Kathmandu Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visitors can explore the surrounding area, which is rich in historical monuments, temples, and palaces. The square offers a glimpse into Nepal's royal history and architectural heritage.

name: Kathekhola -05 Gausara, Baglung Nepal
description: Kathekhola-05 Gausara is a ward within the Kathekhola Rural Municipality in Baglung District, Gandaki Province, Nepal. Kathekhola Rural Municipality, established in 2017, comprises eight wards, with Gausara being one of them. Gausara is known for its picturesque landscapes, including rolling hills, terraced fields, and traditional Nepali architecture. The area offers a glimpse into rural life in Nepal, with opportunities to experience local customs, agriculture, and community activities.

name: Kathmandu Art House
description:
Kathmandu Art House (KAH) is a vibrant center dedicated to Nepalese contemporary and paubha arts, located in the heart of Kathmandu's Thamel district. It serves as a hub for artists, collectors, and art enthusiasts, offering a space to engage with local artists and explore a diverse range of artworks. 


Facilities and Offerings:

Studios and Galleries: KAH houses multiple studios and galleries, providing artists with dedicated spaces to create and exhibit their work. Visitors can explore a variety of art forms, including paintings, sculptures, and mixed-media pieces. 


Art Supplies Store: The center features an art supplies store, catering to the needs of both professional artists and hobbyists. This convenience allows artists to access quality materials on-site. 


Events and Exhibitions: KAH regularly hosts events, exhibitions, and workshops, fostering a dynamic art community. These events provide platforms for artists to showcase their work and for visitors to engage with the local art scene. 


Visiting Information:

Location: Kathmandu Art House is situated in Thamel, Kathmandu, Nepal.

Operating Hours: The center is open daily from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, offering free entry to all visitors

name: Kathmandu Durbar Square
description:
Kathmandu Durbar Square, also known as Hanuman Dhoka Durbar Square, is a historic and cultural landmark located in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal. It served as the royal palace complex for the Malla kings and later the Shah dynasty, making it a significant site in Nepalese history.Historical Significance:

The square has been the center of Kathmandu's political and cultural life for centuries. It was the site where kings were crowned and legitimized, and from where they ruled. Architectural Highlights:

Hanuman Dhoka Palace Complex: This complex includes several courtyards and temples, showcasing traditional Newar architecture. Notable structures within the complex include the Taleju Temple and the Kumari Bahal, the residence of the living goddess, Kumari. 


Temples and Shrines: The square is home to numerous temples, including the Jagannath Temple, the Mahadev Temple, and the Vishnu Temple, each adorned with intricate carvings and sculptures. 


Cultural Significance:

Kathmandu Durbar Square is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its exceptional concentration of monuments and buildings. It exemplifies the fusion of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Tantrism, and remains central to the city today. 


Visitor Information:

Location: Kathmandu Durbar Square is situated in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal.

Operating Hours: The square is open to visitors daily. Please note that there is an entrance fee for foreign visitors. 


Access: The square is accessible by foot from various parts of Kathmandu. It is recommended to hire a local guide to fully appreciate the historical and cultural significance of the site.

name: Kathmandu Fun Park
description:
Kathmandu Fun Park is a prominent amusement park located in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal. It offers a variety of rides and attractions suitable for all ages, making it a popular destination for both locals and tourists.

Attractions and Activities:

Rides: The park features numerous rides, including a Ferris wheel, Columbus, train, tower game, and a dragon coaster. These attractions cater to different age groups, ensuring fun for everyone. 


Additional Amenities: Visitors can enjoy food courts, horse riding, and a horror house. The park is also beautifully landscaped with evergreen trees and flowers, providing a pleasant environment for families.

name: Kathmandu Fun Valley
description:
Kathmandu Fun Valley is a premier recreational destination located in Palase, Bhaktapur, Nepal. It offers a diverse range of water and amusement park attractions suitable for all ages.

Attractions and Activities:

Water Activities: The park features several pools, including a wave pool, a slide pool, and a kids' pool with games. Additional water attractions include a water pendulum and a water pendulum with water flow. 


Amusement Rides: Visitors can enjoy various rides such as the Freezy Columbus, Mini Columbus, Tower Game, Kids Helicopter, Dragon Train, Trampoline, Play Station, Russian Ping, Chand Tara Ping, and Dhikichyaun. 
Facilities: The park also offers a restaurant, fast food stalls, seminar halls, banquet services, and picnic spots. The environment is enhanced with a refreshing green yard, making it an ideal location for family outings.

name: Katikuda
description:
Katakuti is a village development committee located in the Dolakha District of the Janakpur Zone in northeastern Nepal. As per the 1991 Nepal census, it had a population of 3,660 people living in 740 individual households. 

Situated approximately 200 kilometers east of Kathmandu, Katakuti is known for its scenic landscapes and traditional rural lifestyle. The village offers visitors a glimpse into the daily lives of the local communities, who predominantly engage in agriculture and animal husbandry.

For travelers seeking an authentic experience away from urban centers, Katakuti provides opportunities to explore Nepal's rural heritage, interact with indigenous cultures, and enjoy the natural beauty of the region.

Please note that infrastructure in Katakuti may be limited, and amenities such as accommodations and transportation options might not be as readily available as in more developed areas. It's advisable to plan accordingly and consider local customs and practices when visiting.

name: Katunje tole
description:
Katunje is a town located in the Bhaktapur district of Bagmati Province, Nepal. Situated approximately 16 kilometers east of Kathmandu, it lies at an elevation of around 1,339 meters (4,393 feet) above sea level. The town is part of the Kathmandu Valley's inner belt, bordered by urban and semi-rural areas. Its proximity to Bhaktapur Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, adds cultural and historical significance. 

Demographics:

As of the 2011 Nepal census, Katunje had a population of 19,497, residing in 4,692 households. The community is predominantly Newar, known for their unique culture, festivals, and traditional architecture. Other ethnic groups, such as Brahmins, Chhetris, and Tamangs, also reside here. 
Notable Landmarks:

Mahadevsthan Temple: A significant religious site within Katunje.

Ganesh Temple: Another important temple that serves as a focal point for festivals and gatherings.

Sushila Bhairab Temple: A notable temple contributing to the town's cultural heritage.

name: Katyayini Mandir
description:
Religious Site Katyayani Temple, located in Old Baneshwar, Kathmandu, is a significant Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Katyayani, a form of Durga. This temple is revered for its spiritual importance and attracts numerous devotees.
Goddess Katyayani is worshipped as a fierce form of Shakti, known for slaying the buffalo demon Mahishasura. She is considered the sixth among the Navadurga, the nine forms of Durga worshipped during the festival of Navaratri.
The temple features traditional Nepali architectural elements and provides a serene environment for worship and meditation.
The temple serves as a center for various religious activities and rituals, especially during festivals like Navaratri when many devotees visit to seek blessings.
Katyayani Temple is open daily, allowing devotees to make offerings and participate in prayers throughout the year.
Situated in Old Baneshwar, it is easily accessible for both locals and tourists visiting Kathmandu.
Overall, Katyayani Temple holds a prominent place in the spiritual landscape of Kathmandu, embodying the rich traditions of Hindu worship and community engagement.

name: Kaude Lek
description:
Kaude Lek is a scenic hilltop located in the Palpa district of Nepal, near the town of Tansen. Situated at an elevation of approximately 1,500 meters (4,920 feet), it offers panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes, including the Madi Valley, Tansen, Satyawati, and Butwal. 

Attractions and Activities:

Hiking: The journey to Kaude Lek involves a moderate hike, typically taking 30 to 45 minutes from the base. The trail is well-marked and passes through lush forests and traditional villages, providing hikers with a glimpse into local life. 

Photography: The hilltop's vantage point is ideal for capturing the natural beauty of the region, especially during sunrise and sunset.

Cultural Exploration: Visitors can explore nearby villages to experience the local culture, architecture, and cuisine.

Access and Transportation:

To reach Kaude Lek, travelers typically start from Tansen, which is accessible by road from major cities like Butwal and Pokhara. From Tansen, local transportation options such as jeeps or buses can be used to reach the trailhead. It's advisable to check the current road conditions and transportation schedules before planning your visit.

name: Kaudena Bahram Temple
description:
The Kaudena Bahram Temple is a Zoroastrian fire temple located in Nepal. It serves as a place of worship for the Zoroastrian community, following the ancient traditions of fire veneration. The temple is dedicated to Atash Bahram, meaning "Victorious Fire," which is one of the highest-grade fires in Zoroastrianism. This sacred fire is consecrated by sixteen different sources, including the fire created by a lightning bolt. 
Key Features:

Architecture: The temple is constructed in traditional Zoroastrian architectural style, featuring a central fire altar where the sacred fire is maintained. The design reflects the ancient Persian influence, with a focus on simplicity and functionality.

Sacred Fire: The Atash Bahram fire is central to the temple's rituals and is kept burning continuously, symbolizing the presence of Ahura Mazda, the supreme deity in Zoroastrianism.

Cultural Significance: The Kaudena Bahram Temple serves as a spiritual center for the Zoroastrian community in Nepal, preserving and promoting their religious practices and cultural heritage.

Visiting Information:

Location: The temple is situated in a serene environment, offering visitors a peaceful atmosphere for reflection and prayer.

Access: Visitors are welcome to observe the rituals and learn about Zoroastrian traditions. It is advisable to contact the temple authorities in advance to arrange a visit and to understand any specific guidelines or customs to be followed.

name: Kaudena Maharani Mandir
description:
The Kaudena Maharani Mandir is a Hindu temple located in the Kaudena Rural Municipality of Sarlahi District, Province No. 2, Nepal. This temple is dedicated to the worship of the Hindu goddess, Maharani, and serves as a significant religious site for the local community.

Key Features:

Location: Situated in the Kaudena Rural Municipality, the temple is accessible to residents and visitors in the region.

Cultural Significance: The temple plays a vital role in the spiritual life of the local population, hosting various religious ceremonies and festivals throughout the year.

Architecture: The temple's design reflects traditional Nepali architecture, featuring intricate carvings and a serene environment conducive to meditation and prayer.

Visiting Information:

Access: Visitors can reach the temple by traveling to the Kaudena Rural Municipality area, which is well-connected by road to nearby towns and cities.

Best Time to Visit: The temple is open year-round, with special events and festivals occurring during major Hindu holidays.

name: Kavre Roshi
description:
Roshi is a rural municipality located in the Kavrepalanchowk District of Bagmati Province, Nepal. Established on March 10, 2017, through the restructuring of local bodies, Roshi encompasses an area of 176 square kilometers and comprises 12 wards. As of the 2011 Nepal census, it had a population of 28,746. 


Geography and Demographics:

Roshi is situated approximately 27 kilometers east of Kathmandu, the capital city of Nepal. The municipality is predominantly inhabited by the Tamang ethnic group, who speak the Tamang language. Other communities include Magar, Chhetri, Brahmin, Newar, and Thakuri. The area is characterized by its lush green landscapes, rolling hills, and traditional Tamang villages.

Attractions and Activities:

Tindhara Waterfall: Located in the Atrauli area of Roshi, Tindhara Waterfall is a popular destination for both locals and tourists. The waterfall is accessible via a short hike and offers a serene environment for relaxation and picnics. 

Cultural Exploration: Visitors can immerse themselves in the rich Tamang culture by exploring local villages, participating in traditional festivals, and experiencing the unique customs and lifestyles of the community.

name: Kawasoti
description:
Kawasoti is a municipality located in the Nawalpur District of Gandaki Province, Nepal. Situated approximately 31 kilometers west of Bharatpur and east of Butwal, Kawasoti lies along the Mahendra Highway, with the Naryani River flowing to its south and the Mahabharat Range to its north. 


Geography and Demographics:

Area and Population: Covering an area of 114 square kilometers, Kawasoti has a population of approximately 86,821 residents. 

Ethnic Composition: The municipality is home to diverse ethnic groups, including Nepali, Magar, Gurung, and Tharu communities. 


Attractions and Activities:

Chitwan National Park: Located nearby, Chitwan National Park offers opportunities for jeep safaris, canoeing, and forest walks, allowing visitors to experience the rich biodiversity of the region. 

Local Culture: Kawasoti provides a glimpse into the daily life and traditions of the local communities, with various cultural events and festivals celebrated throughout the year.

name: Kawasoti Skate Park
description:
Kawasoti Skate Park is a vibrant recreational facility located in Kawasoti, Nawalpur District, Nepal. Established to provide a safe and engaging environment for skateboarding enthusiasts, the park has become a central hub for the local skateboarding community.

Location and Accessibility:

The skate park is situated approximately 100 meters north of Saphapati Chowk, near the Dragon Fruit intersection. This central location makes it easily accessible to both locals and visitors. 


Facilities and Features:

Skateboarding Areas: The park offers a variety of ramps, rails, and obstacles suitable for skaters of all skill levels.

Community Engagement: Kawasoti Skate Park serves as a gathering place for skateboarders, fostering a sense of community and providing opportunities for skill development and social interaction.

name: Kedareshwor Mahadev Temple
description:
Kedareshwor Mahadev Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, situated in Pokhara, Nepal. Located within the Komagane Friendship Park in the southern part of Lakeside, the temple is easily accessible and offers a serene environment for visitors. 
THE LONGEST WAY HOME

Key Features:

Architecture: The temple is constructed in the traditional Newar pagoda style, featuring red brick walls and intricate wooden carvings. This design mirrors the architectural styles found in the Kathmandu Valley, providing a unique cultural experience in Pokhara. 
THE LONGEST WAY HOME

Main Shrine: At the heart of the temple is a statue of Lord Shiva, the central deity of the worshippers. Adjacent to the main shrine is a statue of Nandi, Shiva's bull, positioned as a traditional guardian figure. 
THE LONGEST WAY HOME

Surroundings: The temple is set within a tranquil park, offering a peaceful retreat from the bustling city life. Visitors can explore the surrounding area, which includes smaller shrines and a well-maintained garden.

name: Keuli Picnic Spot
description:
Keuli Picnic Spot is a popular recreational area located near Butwal in the Lumbini Province of Nepal. Situated approximately 20 kilometers from Butwal, Keuli offers a serene environment ideal for picnics and outdoor activities.

Key Features:

Natural Beauty: The area is characterized by lush greenery, rolling hills, and the tranquil Keuli River, providing a picturesque backdrop for visitors. The riverside setting enhances the spot's appeal, making it a favored destination for both locals and tourists. 

Activities: Visitors can enjoy various activities such as swimming, fishing, and hiking. The calm waters of the Keuli River are suitable for a refreshing dip, while the surrounding trails offer opportunities for exploration.

Facilities: While the area is relatively undeveloped, visitors often bring their own food and supplies for a dry picnic experience. It's advisable to carry essentials like water, snacks, and a first aid kit
address: MHG5+XRP, Unnamed Road, daewadaha nagarapaalaikaa 32900, naepaala

name: Khadak Chowk
description:
hadak Chowk is a notable locality situated in Tikapur, Kailali District, within the Sudurpashchim Province of Nepal. This area is recognized for its vibrant community and serves as a central point in Tikapur. 


Key Features:

Community Hub: Khadak Chowk functions as a central gathering place for residents and visitors, hosting various local events and activities.

Statue of Khadak Bahadur Singh: A prominent feature of the chowk is the statue of the late Khadak Bahadur Singh, a respected figure in the community. This statue serves as a tribute to his contributions and is a point of interest for both locals and tourists. 


Visiting Information:

Accessibility: Khadak Chowk is accessible by road from various parts of Tikapur. Public transportation options are available, and the area is well-connected to other parts of the city.

Nearby Attractions: The chowk is in proximity to several local markets, eateries, and cultural sites, making it a convenient starting point for exploring Tikapur.

name: Khadak bridge
description:
The Khadak Bridge is a notable structure located in the Saptari District of Nepal, specifically over the Khadak River along the Postal Highway at Janjar in Bodebarsain Municipality. This bridge plays a crucial role in connecting various regions, facilitating transportation and commerce.

Recent Developments:

In July 2019, the under-construction Khadak Bridge faced a setback when it collapsed due to flash floods. The floods swept away significant portions of the bridge, leading to a halt in its construction and necessitating extensive repairs

name: Khadbari,pokhari Bazzar
description:
Pokhari Bazar is a notable area within Khandbari, the district headquarters of Sankhuwasabha in eastern Nepal. Khandbari is situated at an elevation of approximately 1,000 meters above sea level, offering a cool climate and scenic views of the surrounding hills. 


Key Features of Pokhari Bazar:

Pokhari Park: A central attraction in Pokhari Bazar is Pokhari Park, a serene spot ideal for relaxation and community gatherings. The park features a pond and is a popular place for both locals and visitors. 


Haat Bazar: Pokhari Bazar hosts a traditional open-air market known as the Haat Bazar. This market operates on specific days and is a vibrant hub where locals trade goods, including fresh produce, handicrafts, and textiles. 

Cultural Significance: The area is rich in cultural heritage, with various festivals and events celebrated throughout the year. These events offer insights into the local traditions and lifestyle of the inhabitants.
